data.name: Imaratun
data.gender_notes: Imaratun is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who commands or rules, Imara means governance or rule and Atun is a feminine name derived from the letter Nun. The name Imaratun carries the meaning “Command, Government, Authority” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Imaratun usually hope their child will grow to embody command, government, authority and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes leadership, governance, and authority in spiritual and worldly matters. Encourages responsibility, compassion, and wisdom.
data.etymology: Imaratun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Command, Government, Authority.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Imaratun total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: عماراتون
in_arabic.meaning: العمارة والبناء، إشارة إلى بناء الجنة

in_urdu.name: عمارتون
in_urdu.meaning: عمارت اور تعمیر، جنت کی تعمیر کا اشارہ

data.cultural_impact: The name "Imaratun" carries a sense of power and authority, which can be attributed to its historical connection to the Islamic concept of Islamic rule or Sharia Law. In various Islamic communities, women have held significant roles in governance and leadership, be it as regents, sultanas, or queens. The name "Imaratun" serves as a reminder of these powerful women and the important leadership roles they have played in Islamic history.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Imaratun" can be seen as a reflection of the inherent leadership role that all individuals hold within their spiritual lives. As believers, each person is expected to govern their own thoughts, words, and actions in accordance with Islamic principles. In this way, every person represents the ruling power of their own lives, guided by the wisdom and command of Allah. Through the name "Imaratun," we are reminded that our power and authority come from our commitment to embodying and living out the divine values and principles of Islam in our daily lives.
